key_insight: VETime fuses vision foundation models with time-series processing by converting signals into visual representations and aligning vision features back to timestamps, enabling zero-shot detection that captures both pointwise and long-range context anomalies.
problem_solved: Bridges the trade-off between 1D temporal models (good at fine-grained localization) and 2D vision models (good at global context) to detect both immediate point anomalies and long-range context anomalies without task-specific labeled data.
method: Visual encoding: transform time series into 2D visual representations (e.g., spectrogram/recurrence-like views) to leverage pretrained vision models.
Temporal alignment module: map vision-derived features back to original timestamps for fine-grained pointwise localization.
Zero-shot anomaly scoring and multi-scale fusion: use pretrained vision foundation models and multi-scale aggregation to identify both local and contextual anomalies without retraining.
impact: Allows ML practitioners to leverage powerful vision foundation models for time-series anomaly detection with minimal or no labeled data, improving detection quality across short-term spikes and long-range contextual shifts while reducing annotation effort.
